clue.text: Ireland's Government pursues EU subsidies in mid-spring

definitions.note: caught in the middle of a leap, as when frolicking

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so the Irish pieces come after the subsidies

parts.note: CAP is the EU's Common Agricultural Policy, its farm subsidy scheme
Erin is the poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Irish government ministers follow the flow of EU farm money in the middle of springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-spring' looks like a season but means midway through a spring or bound.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone leaping playfully about is caught in mid-jump, frisking like a goat.

clue.text: At which point docked horse gets round flower

indicators.note: the horse word surrounds the other piece, getting round it on both sides

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: where means at which point or place

explanation.surface: A horse with a cropped tail circles a bloom in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'horse' as the subject; the wordplay builds the plant name with the trimmed adverb inside the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowherb is a pink-flowered plant of the pink family, a weed of cornfields.

clue.text: Throw out of shape

definitions.note: to throw someone is to disconcert them, an older spelling variant of faze

indicators.note: letters taken out of their shape are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to bend something out of its proper form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw' looks like part of the instruction but is the definition: Chambers gives this spelling as a variant of faze, to disconcert.
explanation.definitionFit: To disconcert or fluster someone is to put them off balance, the sense of faze, of which this is a variant spelling.

clue.text: Non-Indian Hindu following sun-God or his rival?

definitions.note: the demon who swallows the sun, causing eclipses, is the sun's enemy

indicators.note: following places the trimmed Hindu piece after the sun god

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god

indicators.note: the prefix non- removes the following word's letters from Hindu

parts.note: IND is a standard abbreviation for Indian

explanation.surface: A question about a Hindu figure who follows a sun deity or opposes him.
explanation.walkthrough: This Hindu demon is said to swallow the sun in eclipses, so is the sun god's foe; 'Non-' removes IND from Hindu.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu myth this demon pursues the sun and moon, swallowing them to cause eclipses, making it the sun's enemy.

clue.text: Pointless attributing common sense to egghead

parts.note: nous is British informal for practical good sense
the head, or first letter, of egg is E

explanation.surface: It is futile crediting an intellectual with practical sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like a brainy person but means the first letter of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something futile serves no purpose, so it is of no value at all.

clue.text: Taken short, street's toilet for holy man

parts.note: ST is the usual abbreviation for street
john is American slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: A man caught short needs the street's public loo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken short' adds to the toilet picture and, loosely, hints that street is abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint is a holy man, and this is the apostle or evangelist so named.

clue.text: 'Trunk roots' misspelt!

indicators.note: a misspelt word has its letters wrongly arranged, signalling a rearrangement of roots

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the words on a label about trees were spelt wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body, without head or limbs, is the sculptor's word for it.

clue.text: From Bora to Rio, sunbathing works

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A traveller sunbathes from one exotic resort to Rio.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the end of 'Bora' through to the S of 'sunbathing'.
explanation.definitionFit: These are large choral compositions on sacred subjects, musical works like Handel's Messiah.

clue.text: You boy! Turning up prying into other people's business!

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the pieces from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A parent scolds a son who appears and starts snooping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' reverses YESON as a whole, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosy person is inquisitive, poking into affairs that are not theirs.

clue.text: Angry and hurt, flaw being dissected

indicators.note: dissecting cuts something apart, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A person is cross and hurt because a fault is being picked apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of wrath means furious, intensely cross.

clue.text: King surrounded by fools — not much change from the old days!

definitions.text: not much change from the old days

indicators.note: the king letter is placed inside the word for fools, which surrounds it

parts.note: a goat is informal for a fool, as in silly goat
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch among idiots finds the old coinage worth little.
explanation.walkthrough: A groat was an old English silver coin worth fourpence, so small change from past times.
explanation.definitionFit: These old fourpenny silver coins were small change of medieval and later England.

clue.text: Try one out? Neither, as said previously

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of try one are put out of order

explanation.surface: An invitation to try something, met with a refusal in old-fashioned words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an archaic way of saying and not, used where neither once appeared.

clue.text: They're on account of old flames

definitions.meaning: expenses charged to a firm's account, informally shortened

explanation.definitionFit: The word is short for expenses, and also the plural of ex, a former partner.

clue.text: Diabolical study misinterpreted goodly omen

indicators.note: misinterpreting gets things wrong, so these letters come out in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone has misread a happy sign.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the study of demons and devils, so the study of the diabolical.

clue.text: "Cheeky!" — rude response to question about one's age?

parts.note: B is the printed stand-in for a rude word such as bloody

parts.words: response to question about one's age
parts.note: an answer to how old are you might be old

explanation.surface: A rude retort to someone asking your age is cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: The rude reply is 'b— old', B standing for a swear word as printed politely.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward, impudent manner is brazen or cheeky.

clue.text: Salesman's pub brawl with kid

definitions.note: read as salesman is, the 's being a contraction

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a row is a noisy quarrel
a kid is a boy, with simply joining him on

explanation.surface: A salesman gets into a pub fight with a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: A barrow boy is a British street trader selling from a cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A street trader selling fruit or goods from a handcart is a kind of salesman.

clue.text: Pitifully, one's cries decline

indicators.note: something done pitifully is done badly, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Someone's pitiful wailing fades away.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic downturn is a period of decline in activity.

clue.text: Most wicked — as in most excellent!

indicators.note: the first word goes inside the word for most excellent

parts.note: best means most excellent

explanation.surface: A remark that the most evil is also the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: Base means low and immoral, so the superlative is the most wicked.

clue.text: Bit of wood securing plastic with capped pin

definitions.meaning: a small piece cut off timber
a bank card is protected by an embedded microcircuit together with a PIN, in capitals

explanation.definitionFit: A splinter of wood is one sense; the microcircuit in a bank card used with a PIN is the other.

clue.text: No free range here — battery

definitions.meaning: a small cage or prison room gives no freedom to roam
one unit of an electric battery

explanation.definitionFit: A prison room or cage confines its occupant; a single unit of a battery has the same name.

clue.text: Clouds in motion — look out, so's this!

definitions.note: this, the answer, is also clouds in motion: driven vapour

indicators.note: letters in motion are moving about, so the cloud letters are rearranged

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out as storm clouds sweep in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' says LO is taken out: CLOUDS rearranged gives SCUD plus LO. Scud is cloud driven fast by wind, so it too is clouds in motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Scud is light cloud driven swiftly by the wind, so it is itself vapour on the move.

clue.text: To pay for crime gets comfortable

parts.note: to settle a bill is to pay it
a sin is a wrongdoing or crime

explanation.surface: Someone must pay for wrongdoing but is getting comfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer who adapts to a new home or job becomes at ease there.

clue.text: Organic tuna fried with lard, mostly

indicators.note: frying cooks things up, so these letters are tossed together into a new order
most of the word lard is kept, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A recipe for organic fish cooked in lard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims LARD to LAR, which is rearranged with TUNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is grown without synthetic additives, so is free of the artificial.

clue.text: Only hope might be found in a corner here?

definitions.meaning: the final option when all else has failed

definitions.text: might be found in a corner here?
definitions.meaning: a holiday town at the far end of the land, as at a country's corner

explanation.definitionFit: A final remaining option is the sense; the second jokingly reads it as the most remote seaside town.

clue.text: Long and short lights — turn left at end for 22 Across

definitions.note: lands, as a bird alights on a branch

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for short

explanation.surface: Instructions for car headlights on full and dipped, then a direction to turn at the end of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest is a thematic instruction: from the answer's end turn left into 30 Across, whose middle letters complete LANDS END, the 22 Across, Britain's south-western tip.
explanation.definitionFit: To come down and settle, as a bird does on a perch, is to come to earth.

clue.text: Magistrate giving lesson to female malefactor

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school lesson
Eve, the first sinner in Genesis, is the female wrongdoer

explanation.surface: A magistrate gives a moral lesson to a woman offender.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local officer or magistrate in medieval England.

clue.text: I toss horn about

indicators.note: tossing throws things about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An animal boasts of swinging its horn around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' completes the anagram signal and the picture of the beast.
explanation.definitionFit: This horned African beast is known for tossing its horn when charging.

clue.text: He's taken off costume, the fool!

indicators.note: removing these letters is taking them off, as one removes garments

parts.note: costume means clothes
taken as the letters H, E, S

explanation.surface: A man has stripped off his outfit, the idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is British informal for a stupid person.

clue.text: Early reception in bank

definitions.meaning: a morning assembly of visitors held by a monarch on rising
an embankment built against a river

explanation.definitionFit: A royal morning gathering is one sense; a river embankment is the other.

clue.text: With no mister to hold her, Bette's inactive

indicators.note: with no means the following letters are taken away

parts.note: Bette Midler is the American singer and actress

explanation.surface: A woman named Bette, with no man in her life, is at a loose end.
explanation.walkthrough: MR stands on either side of the remaining letters in MIDLER, so it holds her as the clue says.
explanation.definitionFit: To be idle is to be doing nothing, unoccupied or lazy.

clue.text: Dubious denial exposed as false

indicators.note: something dubious is unsound, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A doubtful denial was shown to be a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie that has been pinned down is shown up, as when a falsehood is caught.

clue.text: Penalise Indian involved in half-hearted aggro

indicators.note: the Indian piece is put inside the other, involved within it
half of the heart, the doubled middle letter, is removed

parts.note: bovver is British slang for aggressive trouble-making
IND is a standard abbreviation for Indian

explanation.surface: Someone is punished after getting mixed up in some half-hearted aggression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' takes one of the two middle letters out of the slang word, not literally half of it; BOVVER is British slang for aggro.
explanation.definitionFit: A court may bind someone over, placing them under legal obligation to keep the peace, as a penalty.

clue.text: Poster of series about to finish

indicators.note: the series abbreviation goes round the word for finish

parts.note: to end is to finish

explanation.surface: A billboard advertises that a TV series is about to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poster' looks like a placard but means one who posts something.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who posts a letter dispatches it, so is the one who sends.

clue.text: Sounds like Scottish city will have a stitch-up

indicators.note: the answer is said like the words that follow

parts.note: Dundee is a city in Scotland, and will contracts to 'll

explanation.surface: A Scottish city is going to get an arranged fix.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrangement agreed in advance with no room to change is a fix or stitch-up.
